title: Resonant excitations via low frequency pumping in driven magnon systems
authors: Jan Mathis Giesen, Alexandre Abbass Hamadeh, Imke Schneider, Philipp Pirro, Sebastian Eggert
abstract: We analyse resonant excitations of ferromagnetic magnons via microwave pumping using Floquet theory. Special focus is put on driving frequencies that are below the corresponding magnon energy, which can be excited in large parameter regions via parametric resonances. We develop a theoretical framework that analytically predicts the regions of resonances and resonance thresholds in thin films of ferro- and ferri-magnetic materials like YIG as a function of damping, amplitude and frequency. Resonance regions are separated by exceptional points of the quasi-energies and the results are compared with micromagnetic simulations. The corresponding threshold amplitudes can be estimated from a characteristic powerlaw with damping, leading to the possibility of targeted exciatations at selected wavenumbers using low frequency drive.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how low-frequency microwave pumping can induce resonant excitations in ferromagnetic magnons within thin films like YIG. Using Floquet theory and perturbation methods, the authors predict specific resonance conditions and calculate the critical driving amplitudes required to excite these modes. The findings offer a pathway for targeted control of quantum magnetic states using external electromagnetic fields.
main_problem: The study analyzes resonant excitations of ferromagnetic magnons driven by low-frequency microwave pumping, focusing on parametric resonances occurring when driving frequencies are below the natural magnon energy.
main_result: The theory predicts regions of parametric resonance and determines threshold amplitudes for excitation, showing a characteristic power-law dependence on damping. These results are compared with micromagnetic simulations.
method: The primary methods involve applying Floquet theory to analyze time-periodic systems, utilizing degenerate perturbation theory in the resulting quasi-energy spectrum, and comparing these analytical predictions against full micromagnetic simulations solving the LLG equation.
model_or_system: The system modeled is thin films of ferro- or ferri-magnetic materials like YIG. The dynamics are governed by an effective spin-$S$ Heisenberg model Hamiltonian, analyzed using linear spin wave approximations and bosonic operators.
key_observables: Quasi-energies ($\epsilon$), resonance thresholds ($h_{th}$), instability regions ($	ext{Im}(\epsilon)>0$), and magnon density increase above the threshold.
important_parameters: Damping constant ($\alpha$), microwave driving amplitude ($h_1$), and driving frequency ($\omega_D$). Resonance conditions are linked to $\omega_D = 2\omega_k/n$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the linear spin wave approximation, the uniform-mode approximation, and perturbative expansions for small or intermediate driving amplitudes; higher-order magnon-magnon scattering is neglected in the analytic models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate analytical quasi-energies vs. numerical solutions showing resonance structure (Fig 1), stability charts mapping instability regions ($	ext{Im}(\epsilon)>0$) vs. drive parameters (Fig 2, Fig 4), and simulation results comparing magnon dispersion below and above the predicted threshold (Fig 5).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the Hamiltonian and linear spin wave framework to applying Floquet theory for time-periodic driving. It then develops analytical predictions for resonance thresholds using perturbation theory, addresses strong driving fields via gauge transformations involving Bessel functions, and concludes by comparing these findings with full micromagnetic simulations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses advanced techniques from periodically driven quantum systems (Floquet theory) to model collective excitations in magnetic materials, providing a theoretical framework for controlling magnon dynamics using external fields.
